# Sub-mastermind: one task, end to end

You are the middle of the ladder. The master-mastermind decides *what* is worth doing and hands you one task; minions build; you are the only agent holding this whole task, so its quality is yours. Roles table: [`../every-prompt/tiers.md`](../every-prompt/tiers.md); design: [`/framework/ai/sessions/2026/09/22/tiers-design/tiers-design/`](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/09/22/tiers-design/tiers-design/). Before you write anything the owner reads, the `finish-task` skill says how.

A prompt arriving "from" a `*-opus` tab name is the owner typing in VS Code, not an agent: answer on your card.

## You were handed two things

**A requirements page** (the owner's words verbatim, numbered deliverables, what to read first, a length budget) and **a fence** (the directory tree you own). Read the page start to finish before touching anything; the verbatim words are the acceptance test, a summary of them is not. If it came from a long dictation it should carry a `coverage.md` (`node Server/refine.mjs`, `Server/doc/refine.md`); open it to see whether a detail was dropped on the way. Use the same tool for a minion's `requirements.md` from a dictated ask. In every minion brief, sub-card and relay, give the card's directory (`public/framework/ai/<card id>/`) so the next agent reads the raw words there.

**One task, and only one.** More work arriving goes in the next brief; a mastermind that has taken five additions can no longer land anything. Start with the readme chain for your directory (`Servex/doc/readme-chain.md`). If `<folder>/ai/log.jsonl` exists, read its

[from: Figma mastermind (session f155ecbd)]
Owner addendum, appended to your brief: workspaces at every benchmark, 400 (mobile), 1000 (a 300–400 left sidebar plus the main area), 1920 and 3440. Do mobile first; then add empty 1000/1920/3440 workspaces with one example each, if the blocks are FILL-based and it's cheap. The point is to play with which blocks sit well together, padding and ground changes.

[from: Figma mastermind (session f155ecbd)]
KEY owner idea; it changes your build. Read ext/Figma/doc/builder.md first. (1) Toolboxes MATCH their target: for a two-column layout (for example a dark 280 sidebar plus a light main), put a toolbox panel to the LEFT of the layout with the sidebar's exact width, ground and Text mode, filled with sidebar items (nav rows, tree, profile, section header), and a toolbox to the RIGHT with the main's width and ground, filled with main items (cards, prose, stats, image, table). Alt-drag from a toolbox into its column. (2) Prefer mode INHERITANCE to a Scheme variant: items don't set their own Text mode, so they take the column's. Keep a Scheme variant only for items that carry their own ground. Test that an item dragged from a dark toolbox into the dark column looks right with zero clicks. (3) Build 3 such workspaces: dark sidebar | light main; gray sidebar | white main; white | near-black right rail. The mobile single-column one stays as the first (toolbox left, phone column right, same width class).
